explain.narrative:
## Generic Methods, Bounds and Wildcards

Generic methods declare type parameters before the return type. Bounds restrict acceptable types. extends is useful for producers and super for consumers.

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failures and state assumptions clearly.

Compile with JDK 21, predict output before running, and test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { static <T extends Number> double sum(java.util.List<T> values) { double total=0; for(T value:values) total+=value.doubleValue(); return total; } System.out.println(sum(java.util.List.of(2,3,4))); } }
examples.explanation: A bounded type parameter allows Number methods.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { static <T> T first(java.util.List<T> values) { return values.get(0); } System.out.println(first(java.util.List.of("red","blue"))); } }
examples.explanation: A generic method returns the same type supplied by its list.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { static double total(java.util.List<? extends Number> values) { double sum=0; for(Number n:values) sum+=n.doubleValue(); return sum; } System.out.println(total(java.util.List.of(1,2,3))); } }
examples.explanation: An extends wildcard allows reading Number values from a producer.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { static void addOne(java.util.List<? super Integer> values) { values.add(1); } java.util.List<Number> values = new java.util.ArrayList<>(); addOne(values); System.out.println(values); } }
examples.explanation: A super wildcard accepts a consumer list that can store Integer values.

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { static <T> void show(T value) { System.out.println(value.getClass().getSimpleName()); } show("Java"); } }
examples.explanation: A generic method infers its type argument from the call.
